name: Mau teaches Thompson
summary: Mau Piailug taught Nainoa Thompson and others to combine wind, waves, swells, birds and stars to navigate, passing Micronesian wayfinding to Hawaiian voyagers.
description: Mau taught Nainoa Thompson and collaborators to integrate wind, waves, swells, birds and stars in wayfinding.
tier_reason: Prefer practice and retain the teaching episode. It is a real transmission role, not a duplicate craft or an artifact. This is a scoped consequence judgement, not a reward for documentation or representation.

date.basis: Kyselka dates Thompson’s Micronesia visit to March 1979; PVS dates Mau’s return to Hawaiʻi to teach in that year.

events.statement: Mau taught Nainoa Thompson and collaborators to integrate wind, waves, swells, birds and stars in wayfinding.
events.caveats: This is a dated teaching episode, not the first creation or entirety of either community’s knowledge.

date.label: March–June 1980
date.basis: Participant report locates the actual voyage in March–June 1980; exact first application of this cue or teaching is not established.

events.statement: Thompson used learned wind, wave and celestial wayfinding cues during the 1980 Hōkūleʻa voyage, on which Mau also provided support.
events.population: Nainoa Thompson and the 1980 Hōkūleʻa voyaging crew
events.caveats: Teaching and use are distinct; this does not prove full transfer of Mau’s knowledge or that the voyage was unaided.
